FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: the fee is stated at the level the statute allows and the waiver route is stated twice over. In-window, art. 102.0061(c) requires the fee to be waived unless the art. 55A.151 bar applies, and the packet tells the participant to say so at the counter and cite it. Out-of-window, a district court charges the ordinary county civil ex parte filing fee, which is not a flat statutory amount, and a justice or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. The art. 55A.254(e) and (f) structure is carried as the cost it really is: free electronic transmission, $25 for each listed entity that cannot receive one, repeated at the order stage, so a duplicated or paper-only agency costs $25 twice. The waiver route is the statewide Statement of Inability bound into this packet, with Rule 145's requirement that the clerk supply it free and unasked. The packet refuses to quote the repealed art. 102.006 range and says why. Every one of those statements matches the registry's rules.fees.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: The instructions name the court the route names: 'File the petition with the CLERK OF THE COURT THAT SENTENCED YOU or placed you on community supervision. That clerk forwards it to the court.' They add the statutory filing methods under Sec. 411.0745(a) - in person, electronically or by mail - and say why the proposed order travels with the petition (OCA instructions say most courts require it submitted together). The composed page 9 and page 24 both repeat the direction to ask the clerk of the court being filed in.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: This is the obligation this family handles best, and it handles it the way the owner's standing rule wants. It publishes no figure as its own: 'Sec. 411.0745(b) says the petition must be accompanied by payment of a fee THAT GENERALLY APPLIES TO THE FILING OF A CIVIL CASE... that subsection sets the TYPE of fee, not an amount', OCA describes the total as 'TYPICALLY ABOUT $280, VARYING BY COUNTY', and the direction is 'SO CALL THE CLERK OF THE COURT YOU ARE FILING IN'. It then does something better than silence about the wrong number in circulation: 'NOW THE NUMBER TO IGNORE: $28... THAT FIGURE IS NOT YOURS. It belongs only to the no-petition route under Government Code Sec. 411.072(c).' Both figures and both framings are in data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/TX.memo.json in those terms. The waiver route is the Rule 145 Statement of Inability, which is IN the packet on the statewide bilingual form approved in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and the guide states that Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available 'WITHOUT CHARGE AND WITHOUT YOUR HAVING TO ASK'.

SERVICE.finding: Who and how, and the statute-versus-practice tension stated rather than smoothed. 'WHO GIVES NOTICE TO THE STATE - AND IT IS NOT YOU. Under Sec. 411.0745(e), on receipt of your petition THE COURT provides notice to the State and an opportunity for a hearing.' Then the practical limb: OCA instructions direct a petitioner to show proof the district attorney received a copy and some counties expect it, which is why a proof-of-delivery page ships marked CONDITIONAL with 'ASK THE CLERK' on its own face. The page names no district attorney and no address, and says why: the platform holds none for any Texas county and does not guess one.

officialFormSliceCharacterIdentity.asked: Confirm the official form slice is character-identical to the pinned binary.
officialFormSliceCharacterIdentity.answer: CONFIRMED, and proved at the byte level rather than by comparing extracted text.
officialFormSliceCharacterIdentity.method: For each of the three pinned source binaries, every page's content streams were inflated and compared, stream by stream and byte for byte, against the corresponding delivered page's content streams in BOTH fixtures. 20 source pages x 2 fixtures = 40 page comparisons.
officialFormSliceCharacterIdentity.result: Every delivered official page is one of exactly two shapes. IDENTICAL_NO_OVERLAY (petition pages 2, 3, 4 and Statement source page 10, in both fixtures): the delivered page's content stream array is the source's, unchanged, with nothing added. SOURCE_VERBATIM+OVERLAY (every other official page): the array is exactly ['q\n', ...the source's own streams in their original order, each byte-identical..., 'Q\n', one overlay stream]. row.rulingApplied: The rule I applied to all fifteen, stated once and applied without exception: a route trailer printed below an execution or certification line is a visible CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP defect when the page's own words leave it inside a block the page assigns to the court or to another third party — that is, when NO page-authored line stands between the execution line and the trailer to return the page to the preparer's voice. Where such a line stands there, the page has shown on its own face that the band below the signature is the preparer's, and the trailer — which this corpus draws uniformly on the last page of EVERY component, order and petition and certificate of service and instructions alike (measured here: the pages carrying a trailer are exactly the last page of each component in all fifteen families) — is packet apparatus outside the court's block. The precedent rows are evidence for this rule and not an instruction: VF04 on ri_first_offender_felony-set and VF06 on ri_multiple_misdemeanors-set both turned on the trailer standing inside a Rhode Island block the page declares is the Court's, and that fact is present here for ri_decriminalized-set and absent for the twelve I pass. If the Captain instead rules the component-closer convention itself unacceptable anywhere inside a proposed order, all fifteen follow the same way and the twelve passes become fails; I say so rather than hide the sensitivity.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.evidence: The filing-instructions component states: art. 102.006 repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 with a built-in expiry, permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01; under (a) a district court charges the ordinary county civil ex parte fee with no flat amount, under (b) a justice or municipal court of record charges a flat $100; under (c) the fee MUST be waived in-window where art. 55A.151 does not apply, and under (d) where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B); art. 55A.254(e) forbids a charge for electronic transmission and (f) requires $25 per listed entity unable to receive one, repeating at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3); the Statement of Inability under Rule 145 is in the packet and the clerk must supply it free. Every clause is in TX.memo rules.fees and rules.feeWaiver. The packet also refuses the repealed $250-to-$500 range and says why. Nothing is denied that the repository holds.

SERVICE.evidence: 'YOU DO NOT SERVE ANYONE. THE CLERK DOES. SELF_HELP_STOP.evidence: A section headed 'When to stop and get help instead' carries all TWELVE selfHelpStopConditions from data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json track tx_exp_acquittal. observationsNotAffectingTheVerdict: participant-instructions.md and the filing-instructions component both say 'A certificate of service is included only where local practice requires you to serve the prosecutor directly - ask the clerk.' No certificate of service is in this packet: the manifest names six components and none is one, and TX.memo's own components[] names none either. The sentence is a carry of the memo's rules.service prose into a document that is describing its own contents, and a participant in such a county will look for a page that is not there. It is not failed here because no required component is missing, the substantive service rule is stated correctly, and the packet's authoritative self-description — its component table — does not list one. The sibling family tx_nd_conviction_no_supervision-set handles the identical situation properly by shipping a conditional proof-of-delivery component and saying so. Cheapest repair: reword to 'this packet does not include a certificate of service; ask the clerk whether that county requires you to serve the prosecutor directly and to prepare one.'

The verified ex parte petition and the proposed order both open with instructional prose addressed to the filer — 'USE THIS PAGE IF THE 30-DAY WINDOW HAS CLOSED', 'NOTE WHERE THIS ONE GOES', 'USE THIS PAGE ON THE OUT-OF-WINDOW BRANCH ONLY' — and the proposed order carries the two route keys as a printed footer. These are documents that get filed with a district clerk. This is the factory's established custom-pleading house style rather than a defect of this family, and it is recorded so that whoever owns that style decides it once rather than per family.

FILING_DESTINATION.evidence: 'File the petition with the CLERK OF THE COURT THAT SENTENCED YOU. That clerk forwards it to the court. Under Government Code Sec. 411.0745(a) you may file it in person, electronically or by mail. OCA instructions say that in most courts a proposed order must be submitted with the petition.' TX.memo rules.filing and destination.name say exactly that, including the one-order-per-offence rule, which the packet also carries.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.evidence: 'Sec. 411.0745(b) … sets the TYPE of fee, not an amount … your county's civil filing fee schedule governs. OCA instructions describe the total as TYPICALLY ABOUT $280, VARYING BY COUNTY, and tell you to call the clerk.' And on the number that is not theirs: 'NOW THE NUMBER TO IGNORE: $28 … It belongs only to the no-petition route under Government Code Sec. 411.072(c), and the committed record states in terms that it is not a filing fee at all … Do not arrive at the clerk's window with $28.' TX.memo rules.fees states precisely this, including the $28 disclaimer. Waiver: Rule 145 Statement of Inability on the Misc. Docket 22-9090 statewide form, in the packet, with the clerk's duty to supply it free and unasked. Nothing denied that the repository holds.

SERVICE.evidence: 'WHO GIVES NOTICE TO THE STATE - AND IT IS NOT YOU. Under Sec. 411.0745(e), on receipt of your petition THE COURT provides notice to the State and an opportunity for a hearing … OCA instructions do direct a petitioner to show proof that the district attorney received a copy, and some counties expect it, which is why this packet includes a proof-of-delivery page marked CONDITIONAL. Ask the clerk whether that county wants it.' Matches TX.memo rules.notice and rules.service, and unlike the sibling family the conditional document it describes is actually in the packet, at page 9.

SELF_HELP_STOP.evidence: A section headed 'When to stop and get help instead' in participant-instructions.md, repeated in the filing-instructions component. All seven selfHelpStopConditions in TX.memo track tx_nd_conviction_no_supervision are covered in substance: community supervision (wrong section), violent-or-sexual characterisation under § 411.0735(c-1) with the Penal Code § 22.01 carve-out named, incomplete or uncertain sentence completion, any other conviction or deferred adjudication beyond a fine-only traffic offence, prosecutor opposition or hearing request, family violence finding OR allegation, and immigration ('you are not a United States citizen'). It then names who answers what where self-help stops.

observationsNotAffectingTheVerdict: The packet says the sealed information 'is still disclosed to the individuals and agencies listed in Government Code Sec. 411.076(a)'. TX.memo's own participant-facing limitation names Gov't Code § 411.0765 and lists the categories concretely — school districts, charter and private schools, education service centres, commercial transportation companies — and adds that the person may not deny the matter in those contexts. § 411.076(a) does carry the list by reference to § 411.0765, so the citation is not wrong, but the concrete categories the memo wanted the participant to see are not in the packet. Not failed: nothing held is denied.

The post-order mechanics the packet states — clerk to DPS by the 15th business day, DPS onward within 10 business days to the § 411.075(b) recipients, those recipients sealing within 30 business days — are all in TX.memo. Checked because a filing-critical number that is not in a held record is how a packet invents one. Every one of them is held.

residualProvenanceConflictRecordedNotSco.what: The packet tells the participant, in capitals, 'IF YOU HAVE READ THAT EXPUNCTION COSTS $250 TO $500, THAT RANGE IS FROM THE REPEALED STATUTE AND THIS PACKET WILL NOT REPEAT IT', and the instructions repeat it as 'The $250-to-$500 range that circulates online comes from the repealed statute'. NO HELD RECORD SAYS THE RANGE COMES FROM ART. 102.006. The committed track registry says only that the packet does not quote 'the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable'. The compiled Texas profile attributes it to something else entirely: in filingDestinationRules, describing step 4 of this very route, it records 'File in a district court for the county of arrest or prosecution (Art. 55A.251). Pay the civil filing fee, which varies by county (often roughly $250-$500 for expunction in many counties; some are lower)'. That is a description of the COUNTY CIVIL FILING FEE — which is exactly the fee art. 102.0061(a) makes applicable in district court, the same fact and the same route, so A3 does not exclude it.
residualProvenanceConflictRecordedNotSco.whyItDoesNotFailTheObligation: A1 asks the route-specific record first, and the committed track registry directs the exclusion in terms. A packet that obeys its controlling record is not failing for obeying it. The obligation is met on limb one regardless: the fee rule is stated and sourced, the mandatory waiver is stated with its subsection, and the Rule 145 form ships.
residualProvenanceConflictRecordedNotSco.whatIsActuallyWrong: The provenance clause is an unsourced assertion printed to a participant, and it conflicts with the compiled profile. A reader who checks will find the range attached to county civil filing fees, not to art. 102.006, and will not be able to tell which record to believe.
residualProvenanceConflictRecordedNotSco.raisedNotDecided: Flagged for Captain rather than scored, in the shape A3 itself was raised. Two held records describe one figure differently and the packet picks a third description. Whether a lane may fail FEE_AND_WAIVER on a false provenance clause when the fee rule itself is right is a yardstick question, not a reading question, and this lane will not settle it alone.

Step 4 of participant-instructions.md tells the participant in terms: 'Mark the three controls on the petition yourself: whether the evidence of completion is attached, which waiting period applies, and whether you are paying the fee or filing the Statement of Inability.' On the delivered bytes the option boxes carry only the form's own empty-box glyph (U+F06F, the source form's unmarked box) and no mark. requiredOptionsMissing measured 0. The 44 further blanks classified PARTICIPANT_ELECTION_GENUINE on the Statement of Inability are its benefit and household election boxes, all likewise unmarked, with the field map's reason recorded: the platform holds no financial or household fact and will not mark a box on a sworn financial affidavit.

REPEATING_ROWS.finding: Measured rather than assumed. The completeness contract's row detector, run here over this family's own field map, keys 33 cells into 5 named rows — Row1 through Row5 of the Statement of Inability's dependants table (Name, age and relationship cells). Every cell of every one of the five rows is a declared refusal and every one is blank on the delivered bytes of both fixtures, so no row is partially filled and incompleteRows measures 0. Instrument limit stated: the detector keys on named Item/Row/Line segments, so the Statement's income, property, monthly expense and debt tables — whose fields are not named with a row segment — are not counted as rows. This lane checked them anyway: the family writes nothing financial at all (all 8 Statement writes are identity fields), so those tables are uniformly blank and cannot contain a half-filled row either.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.finding: A field this packet declares protected, for the reason that filling it would make the document false, is delivered carrying ink. The field map declares tx_nd_dwi_probation-fee-waiver-statement-4.Today with refusalClass signature_or_date_participant_completion and the stated reason 'a date written before the Statement is actually sworn would be false'. Its widget rect, read first-hand from the pinned binary, is x 97.75 y 302.31 w 150 h 22 on source page 11 of the Statement, which is packet page 20. Extracting word geometry there returns the word '12/15/2022' at xMin 99.75 yMin 474.52 xMax 159.80 yMax 485.62, which converts to inside that rectangle on every edge. It sits directly above the printed caption 'Date (month, day, year) / Fecha (mes, día, año)', immediately beside the participant's signature line, on the page whose own heading is the sworn declaration under penalty of perjury. It is present in both the canonical and the boundary artifact. This lane also established where it comes from, so the repair is not misdirected: the build did not write it. '12/15/2022' is present in the byte-exact official source PDF itself (private/human-source-returns/TX/TX__STATEMENTOFINABILITYTOAFFORDPAYMENTOFCOURTCOSTSO.pdf, SHA-256 bd17a3fe43d6989d1828c91c9a46c873908c272d8e2e342af35ce8bdb2fab10d, which this lane rehashed byte-exact) as that form's own baked appearance for its 'Today' field. The family's report says refusedFieldsWithInk: [] and that is true of ink the finalizer added; it cannot see ink the source carried, which is why no counter reports this. The defect is that the packet's own declaration and its own delivered bytes disagree about the same field, and nothing tells the participant: 'Things the platform deliberately left blank' names the financial facts and the cause number on the Statement, and says nothing about a date already printed on the sworn declaration. A participant following these instructions signs a sworn statement bearing a date three and a half years stale. Recorded to keep the classification honest: the three other refused fields whose boxes contain glyphs — Choice 1, Group10 and Group12 — contain only U+F06F, the source form's own unmarked-checkbox glyph, which is the box itself and not a mark. They are correct and are not part of this failure.

PAGE_ORDER.finding: packetPage runs 1..24 with no gap or repeat in both fixtures. All five components occupy contiguous blocks in manifest order with sourcePage monotonic inside each, and each block's page count equals the page count of the source it binds: petition 5 pages against the 5-page OCA petition, proposed order 3 against the 3-page OCA order, proof of delivery 1 composed page, fee waiver statement 12 against the 12-page Statement, filing instructions 3 composed pages. Read on the bytes the order is the order a filer needs: petition, order for the judge, the conditional proof of delivery, the conditional fee-waiver Statement, then the instructions that explain all four.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: Word geometry extracted with pdftotext -bbox-layout and EVERY same-baseline pair classified, which matters here because this is the only family in the roster with any. 30 pairs in the canonical artifact and 37 in the boundary artifact. All 67 classify as a written value sitting on the underscore rule that receives it — for example 'Jordan' / 'Avery' / 'Reyes' on the petition's Printed Name rule at page 1, and the boundary participant's 'Maria-Alejandra' / "O'Shaughnessy-Whitfield" on the same rule and on the Statement's name rule at page 11. Zero pairs are value-on-value. This lane then checked containment as well as classification: for every one of the 67 pairs the value's horizontal extent lies inside the rule's horizontal extent, so 0 of 67 values overrun the rule that receives them. Zero words fall outside the page box in either fixture. No value was refused at the 6pt floor with a blank left for the participant, so the Lane C correct-refusal case did not arise. This instrument cannot see raster ink, vector rules, field borders, images, or glyphs without extractable text — which on this family means it cannot see the official forms' own printed rules and boxes except where they extract as underscore runs; the raster receipt cited above reports 0 problems over 48 rendered pages and no pixel of it was inspected here.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: Held and stated. The census and registry record destination 'The court that sentenced the person or placed the person on community supervision, filed through its clerk'. The delivered instructions page states it and adds the filing mechanics the registry holds: 'File the petition with the CLERK OF THE COURT THAT SENTENCED YOU or placed you on community supervision. That clerk forwards it to the court. Under Government Code Sec. 411.0745(a) you may file it in person, electronically or by mail. OCA instructions say that in most courts a proposed order must be submitted with the petition, which is why the proposed order is in this packet.' It also carries the registry's one-offence-one-order rule. The caption's court and county blanks are both disclosed in the instructions table with what to write. Nothing the record answers is delegated.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: POSITIVE FINDING — the strongest A3 application in this roster, and one a repair lane must not flatten. The packet does not merely refuse a figure; it names the figure the participant will have seen, says whose route it belongs to, and tells them not to bring it: 'NOW THE NUMBER TO IGNORE: $28. You may have read that an order of nondisclosure costs $28. THAT FIGURE IS NOT YOURS. It belongs only to the no-petition route under Government Code Sec. 411.072(c), and the committed record states in terms that it is not a filing fee at all. This is a petition route under Sec. 411.0731. Do not arrive at the clerk's window with $28.' It then states what IS held: § 411.0745(b) sets the TYPE of fee and not an amount, so the county civil filing fee schedule governs; OCA describes the total as typically about $280 varying by county; call the clerk of the court you are filing in. That reproduces the registry's rules.fees, which records exactly this and records the $28 as belonging to § 411.072(c). The waiver limb is a delivered component, not a sentence: the packet ships the statewide bilingual Statement of Inability approved in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090 and states that Rule 145 requires the clerk to make that form available without charge and without the participant having to ask. Two records are worth noting together: the registry carries a releaseBlocker on the county figure, and the packet honours it by quoting the OCA range rather than inventing a county number. A4 is satisfied and then some — the packet states two dollar figures and correctly characterises each.

evidence.figureStatedAndAttributed: $280 typical per OCA, varying by county
evidence.figureRefusedAndAttributed: $28, belonging to the no-petition route under § 411.072(c)
evidence.namedCheckableAuthority: the clerk of the court you are filing in
evidence.doNotRepairThisBy: replacing the OCA range with a single county figure, or deleting the $28 paragraph

SERVICE.finding: Stated, and stated in the direction that protects the participant from doing work that is not theirs. The packet says: 'WHO GIVES NOTICE TO THE STATE - AND IT IS NOT YOU. Under Sec. 411.0745(e), on receipt of your petition THE COURT provides notice to the State and an opportunity for a hearing. The committed record states that you should not be charged for that notice. OCA instructions do direct a petitioner to show proof that the district attorney received a copy, and some counties expect it, which is why this packet includes a proof-of-delivery page marked CONDITIONAL. Ask the clerk whether that county wants it.' That reproduces the registry's rules.notice and rules.service including the tension between the statute and the OCA instructions, resolves it structurally by shipping the proof-of-delivery page as conditional rather than required, and names the authority who settles it locally. The packet separately refuses to print a district attorney name or address, recording that the platform holds neither for any Texas county.

evidence.namedCheckableAuthority: the clerk of the county being filed in

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Three of the eight self-help stop conditions the committed record establishes for this track are absent from the delivered packet and from participant-instructions.md. The registry entry tx_nd_dwi_probation carries eight conditions, identically in selfHelpStopConditions and selfHelpBoundaries. The packet's stop list is not derived from them: it is hard-coded as seven bullets at scripts/build-census-v1-tx_nd_dwi_probation-set.mjs lines 721-728, and the same seven appear in participant-instructions.md. Comparing condition by condition and grepping each condition's distinguishing terms against the extracted text of BOTH fixtures and the instructions file: (1) 'The prosecutor opposes the petition or requests a hearing' — ABSENT. 'opposes' returns 0 in both fixtures and the md; the packet discusses hearings only descriptively, telling the participant that if the State stays silent for 45 days there may be no hearing at all, which is procedural information and not a stop. (2) 'Any dispute about whether the sentence, fines, costs or restitution were completed' — ABSENT. 'dispute' returns 0; the packet's only nearby statement runs the other way, reassuring that 'YOU REMAIN ELIGIBLE IF THE COURT WAIVED YOUR FINES AND COSTS'. (3) 'Any question whether the offence was violent or sexual in nature, which is a court determination under Gov't Code 411.0735' — ABSENT, and this is the one that costs most. '411.0735' returns 0 in both fixtures and the md; 'violent' returns 0; 'sexual in nature' returns 0. The two hits for 'sexual' in the artifact are inside the OCA form's own § 411.074 exclusion list of offence titles, a different list answering a different question. Nothing anywhere in the packet tells a participant that whether the offence was violent or sexual is a court determination under its own section. Two further conditions are present only in narrowed form and are recorded as supporting, not as the failure: the registry stops on 'Any family violence finding or family violence ALLEGATION anywhere in the record' while the packet stops on 'The court has made an AFFIRMATIVE FINDING of family violence', and the registry stops on 'Any accident ALLEGATION in the offence report' while the packet stops on 'The offence RESULTED IN a motor vehicle collision'. In both the registry reaches an allegation and the packet reaches only an established fact, which is the wrong direction for a stop condition — a stop exists to catch the participant before the question is resolved against them. The remaining three conditions are properly carried, and the packet adds two correct conditions of its own (alcohol concentration 0.15 or higher, and supervision revoked at any point).

absent: The prosecutor opposes the petition or requests a hearing.
Any dispute about whether the sentence, fines, costs or restitution were completed.
Any question whether the offence was violent or sexual in nature, which is a court determination under Gov't Code 411.0735.
evidence.packetStopListIsHardCoded: scripts/build-census-v1-tx_nd_dwi_probation-set.mjs lines 721-728, seven bullets, not derived from the registry

blindSpotAnswered.checkedAnyway: This family is official_pdf_fill rather than a composed pleading, so its caption blanks are AcroForm widgets on the OCA petition rather than a hard-coded dot run. Both are declared refusals with widget rects read first-hand from the pinned binary, both appear in the blanks report, and both are disclosed in the instructions table — 'Court the petition is filed in, named in the caption' with 'the court that sentenced you or placed you on community supervision, exactly as its own paperwork names it', and 'County of that court, named in the caption'. No participant is left to supply a court nobody told them to.
